Building on this insight, this paper investigates the transmission of information in MLLMs, identifying and filtering hallucinated knowledge based on changes in the information flow, thereby mitigating hallucinations from an information-level perspective. We design an effective strategy to track the differences in information between adjacent layers within the model, and find that for hallucinated responses, the model often undergoes significant information mutations in deep layers. We suspect that these inconsistent knowledge does not originate from the input image, and instead is injected directly into the model, which influences the probabilities of hallucinated tokens. To further validate this hypothesis, we analyze the probability changes of hallucinated tokens across different layers. The results reveal that these tokens' probabilities often surge in layers with drastic information changes, becoming dominant and ultimately appearing in the final response, thereby causing hallucinations.
